annotation.title_clean: Data regulation in the age of AI and other data-intensive technologies
annotation.title_en: Data regulation in the age of AI and other data-intensive technologies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology; Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport (UK)
annotation.summary_en: UK government call for evidence on how personal and non-personal data regulation interacts with AI and other data-intensive technologies, including agentic AI, synthetic data and PETs. It asks whether guidance, targeted changes or reform is needed, covering lawful basis, data minimisation, fairness, accuracy and data sharing.
key_provisions_or_claims: Seeks practical evidence on friction between UK data protection law and AI development and adoption.
Themes include lawful bases, data minimisation, purpose limitation, special category data, data quality, accuracy and fairness.
Asks whether further guidance, targeted changes or fundamental reform is needed.
Interested in PETs, synthetic data and agentic AI as future challenges.
Aims to make the UK the fastest-adopting AI economy in the G7 while preserving public trust.
